questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This asks for a branchless, constant-time rotate, common in codecs and crypto; the input n should be reduced via &31 to 0..31.

## Key Concepts
- rotate using shifts and OR
- mask n with 31
- edge-case r=0 yields x
- portability, unsigned behavior

## Code Example
```c
static inline uint32_t rotateLeft32(uint32_t x, unsigned int n){
  unsigned int r = n & 31;
  return (x << r) | (x >> ((32 - r) & 31));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend to 64-bit? 
- How would you test edge cases like r=0, r=31, and large n?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement a rotation primitive with wrap-around using only shifts and masks, including masking to handle large r and the n=0 edge case.

## Key Concepts
- Circular shift using (x << n) | (x >> (32 - n))
- Masking r with 31 to confine to 0..31
- Edge-case n=0 preserves x exactly

## Code Example
```c
static inline uint32_t rotl32(uint32_t x, unsigned r) {
  unsigned n = r & 31; // 0..31
  return (x << n) | (x >> (32 - n));
}
```

- What are the potential performance differences vs. compiler intrinsics like _rotl?
- How would you test across boundary values (r=0, r=31, r=32, r=33)?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to decompose a 128-bit value into fixed lanes and reconstruct a rotated layout using only bitwise ops and masking, without branches.

## Key Concepts
- Lane extraction with masks, 32-bit blocks
- Fixed-layout reconstruction; endianness awareness
- Constant-time block-wise permutation

## Code Example
```javascript
uint128 rotateBlocks128(uint128 x) { uint64_t A = x.lo & 0xFFFFFFFFULL; uint64_t B = (x.lo >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFFULL; uint64_t C = x.hi & 0xFFFFFFFFULL; uint64_t D = (x.hi >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFFULL; uint128 r; r.lo = (A << 32) | D; r.hi = (C << 32) | B; return r; }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to generalize to n blocks or different block sizes?
- How to ensure correctness on little- vs big-endian targets?
- Could you adapt this for a compile-time constant permutation table?
